headline: A dated permission that lapses is a requirement, and a certificate's own extended key usages name the purpose it was issued for.
summary: The Apple Root Program Policy ships as `apple-root`, the last of the four root programs, named and never detected like the others. Its Appendix A defines seven Trust Purposes as extended key usage sets, and its rules are dated: a subordinate CA certificate needs an extKeyUsage extension from 1 August 2026 and must be dedicated to one purpose from 1 July 2027, while a subscriber certificate's permission to mix purposes is written as a permission that expires on that same date.

Added: `pki.lint.certificate(der, { profile: "apple-root" })` runs the Apple Root Program Policy v2.0 profile. Naming it is the only way to reach these rows, and passing no profile leaves every one of them inert.

Appendix A's seven Trust Purposes, each a required extended key usage set: Server Authentication, Legacy TLS, Secure Email, Legacy S/MIME, Client Authentication, Time Stamping and VMC. A certificate is dedicated to a purpose when its extKeyUsage is not empty and names nothing outside that purpose's set, which is how the appendix states it: a subordinate CA "MUST contain only the EKU(s) specified for that Trust Purpose".

The section 1.7 rules over a subordinate CA certificate, each gated on the signing date the clause defines for itself, which it says a renewal, a re-key and a cross-sign each produce afresh. From 1 August 2026 the extKeyUsage extension is required and `anyExtendedKeyUsage` is not permitted. In the window that runs to 1 July 2027 the clause admits either dedication to one purpose or three conditions together, of which one is in the certificate: that it names no extended key usage belonging to a purpose. So a certificate naming one of those identifiers has already failed that arm, and if its set spans two purposes it has failed the other, which is what a single certificate settles. From 1 July 2027 the second arm is gone and dedication is required outright, so a certificate for a use the appendix does not list is reported then and passed over before.

Section 2.3's rule that a subscriber certificate carrying `id-kp-emailProtection` and signed on or after 1 February 2027 names at least one rfc822Name in its subjectAltName, and Appendix A's last note read as what it is: a permission for a subscriber certificate signed before 1 July 2027 to carry extended key usages spanning more than one purpose. A permission bounded by a date binds once the date passes. `anyExtendedKeyUsage` is in scope for that rule even though the appendix's table does not list it, because RFC 5280 section 4.2.1.12 makes it a certificate not restricted to any specific key purpose: it names every purpose rather than none, and conforms to no single one. That is what separates it from a purpose the table does not list at all, such as code signing, which leaves a certificate under no trust purpose and outside the rule.

Section 1.5's floor for a root certificate, an RSA modulus of at least 4096 bits or a curve of at least NIST P-384. The clause names those two families and no others, so a key outside both is reported as well.
`id-kp-BrandIndicatorforMessageIdentification` (`1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.31`) joins the OID registry, under IANA's own spelling for it, so the VMC purpose resolves by name like the other six.
Changed: `pki.lint.rules()` enumerates the new rows, which stay inert under the default rule set because each one asks whether the caller named the profile.
